title: Nocturnal heap and batching playbook
body:
Quick context:
- Night shift notes: noticed repeated small p99 spikes on g4dnx-large around longer sequences (seq_len > 2k). Patterns point to transient heap fragmentation + occasional cudaMalloc stalls. Visible in perf traces as 5–12ms jitter every ~600 requests.

High-level hypothesis:
1) Batching causes VM allocator churn when many small tensors get created/destroyed between token generations.
2) NVLink peer-to-peer mapping + async memcpy interplay triggers intermittent blocking when combined with small batch packing.
3) KV-cache growth + dynamic attention windows cause allocator pressure and fallback to slower allocation path.

Repro notes (lightweight repro to iterate quickly):
- Use local dev box with same docker image (runtime:sha:2026-02-26).
- Run microbench: tests/tooling/mini-latency-run --model redwood-open-7b --seq 2048 --concurrency 12 --batch-policy packing_small.
- Capture with: sh scripts/trace-capture.sh --trace-type cuda-malloc --duration 180s --out /tmp/trace-ravi.gz
- Collect nvprof / nsight summary for suspicious memcpy patterns.

Observations so far (raw):
- cudaMalloc took 1–3ms normally but spikes to 15–30ms when other processes started small pinned copies.
- Free lists show many tiny free blocks (128B–4KB) interleaved with a few huge ones. Fragmentation ratio ~0.48.
- Batching policy packing_small triggers ~40% more allocations vs packing_medium because of per-request padding removal.

Short term mitigations (fast to try):
- Force jemalloc tunables in container: MALLOC_CONF=arenas:1,lg_chunk:20 (reduce arenas to lower fragmentation across threads).
- Add per-worker small-slab caching: enable env VAR: RW_SMALL_SLAB=1 (experimental flag in runtime).
- Change packing policy to packing_medium in staging for the offending model family for 12h and monitor.
- Add a soft backoff: if cudaMalloc latency > 10ms, switch to synchronous fallback path with pre-allocated pool (cheap guard, code in runtime/pool-guard).

Longer experiments (next 1–2 sprints):
- Implement per-GPU bump allocator for tiny tensors (<=4KB) to avoid general allocator overhead. Measure mem overhead vs p99 gain.
- Explore kv-cache pre-reserve heuristics: pre-reserve expected KV growth per request when seq_len > 1024.
- Add NVLink-aware memcpy scheduling: stagger peer-to-peer transfers when packing density > 70% to avoid contention wave.

Immediate TODOs (priority order):
- [ ] Run packing_medium rollout on canary pool for redwood-open-7b (owner: Maya) — target: 24h, check p50/p95/p99 and error rates.
- [ ] Hook jemalloc env in canary image and run overnight load (owner: Ravi) — compare fragmentation metric and malloc hist.
- [ ] Add trace flag to trace-capture.sh to include pci bus saturation stats (owner: Hector).
- [ ] Open small RFC describing per-worker small-slab approach (owner: Ravi) — link to RFC once drafted.

Notes-to-self (quick):
- When reproducing, ensure no background S3 transfers on the same host — they can mask NVLink issues. Use isolated node via gce label: runtime-isolated.
- If you see cudaFree blocking, also inspect whether cudaStreamSynchronize got called on default stream accidentally.
- Look at that odd log line: "cache-resize: triggered from attention-window-extender" — could be an unrelated codepath expanding kv buffer mid-request. Track in INF ticket.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Is fragmentation coming primarily from token->tensor ephemeral allocations, or from attention resizing? Need allocation stack traces to tell.
- Does jemalloc arena reduction hurt multi-threaded throughput on high-concurrency clients? Test with concurrency 24.
- Could enabling tiny-slab increase OOM risk on worst-case sequences? Measure headroom.

Relevant snippets/commands (copyable):
- repro run (dev): docker run --rm -e RW_PROFILE=1 -e MALLOC_CONF=arenas:1,lg_chunk:20 -v /tmp:/tmp rw/runtime:canary /bin/bash -c "python3 tools/mini-latency-run.py --model redwood-open-7b --seq 2048 --concurrency 12 --policy packing_small"
- trace capture: scripts/trace-capture.sh --trace cuda-malloc,cuda-free,nvlink --duration 300 --out /tmp/trace.gz
- quick malloc histogram: python3 tools/alloc-hist.py /tmp/trace.gz | head -n 40

Communication plan:
- Ping runtime-oncall channel if revert needed during canary.
- Post quick findings in #runtime-anomolies with a short summary + p99 numbers. Attach trace link.
- If jemalloc change helps, plan a controlled rollout and update runtime image docs.

End-of-shift signoff checklist (if fixed during shift):
- [ ] Confirm p99 reduced by >=20% on canary for 6h window.
- [ ] Open PR with small-slab guard and tests.
- [ ] Notify SRE/observability to add a metric: allocator-fragmentation-ratio per-host.

Fragmented thought dump (for later):
- Maybe use request-level arena reuse: allocate a request arena and reuse for ephemeral tensors for the duration of request; free at end. Could reduce cross-request fragmentation but may increase peak memory slightly. Worth prototyping as opt-in flag.
- Consider a background compaction thread that coalesces small free blocks during low usage. Tricky but possible on dedicated nodes.

Random TODOs (personal):
- [ ] Draft the RFC by Monday.
- [ ] Remind Maya to try packing_medium on a subset of users with long sequences.
- [ ] Add quick note to release doc about the jemalloc knob and potential perf tradeoffs.

Last checked: 2026-03-11 02:12 UTC (local night-run).
